title: g, h and f in A*

items.stem: A guard NPC starts at tile S. A wall is in the way, so the cheapest path the search has found from S to tile n takes 7 steps, even though n is only 3 tiles from S in a straight line. Every step costs 1. What is g(n)?

options.text: 3, the distance from the start tile S to tile n
7, the cost of the path found from S to tile n
The Manhattan distance from tile n to the goal
10, the 3 tiles of distance plus the 7 steps

items.stem: On a grid where the NPC moves only up, down, left or right, tile n is at (2, 3) and the goal is at (6, 1). What is h(n) if the heuristic is Manhattan distance?
The search is at tile C, and g(C) = 4. Tile N is next to C, the step from C to N costs 1, and h(N) = 3. Going through C is the cheapest path to N found so far. What is f(N)?
Four tiles have these values. Which tile has the smallest f value?

options.text: Tile P, with g = 6 and h = 2
Tile Q, with g = 1 and h = 7
Tile R, with g = 3 and h = 4
Tile T, with g = 2 and h = 6

items.stem: On a grid where the NPC can also move diagonally, a straight step costs 1 and a diagonal step costs 1.4. The path found so far from the start to tile n is 2 straight steps and 3 diagonal steps. What is g(n)?
In one or two sentences: what does f(n) = g(n) + h(n) estimate, and why does A* add g(n) instead of using h(n) alone?
